summary.prose: Building this Story means writing one new module that lays a lock table over a single SharedArrayBuffer and gives every daemon thread a Web Locks-shaped request/query API on it, with waiting done by Atomics.waitAsync and every state change behind a short per-name mutex. The work goes bottom-up: block layout and validation, then grants and release, then waiting with timeout and abort, then query and reclaim for dead workers. It ends by making the lock block a required part of every daemon worker's start and proving the semantics across real worker threads, including workers killed in the middle of a grant.

tasks.title: Lock block layout, name table, install and errors
tasks.summary: Create src/shared/locks/lock-manager.ts with the block layout (header with capacities and acquisition counter; name table with claim state storing the claimer threadId, hash, length and 64 name bytes; per-name lock word, pending-exclusive count, version word and mutex word; holder and pending tables), createLockBlock(capacity?) with defaults 64/512/256, installLockManager(block) and getLockManager() (private block outside a daemon, as getStoreGuard), the error classes LockTimeoutError, LockNestedError, LockCapacityError and LockArgumentError, argument validation (name 1-64 UTF-8 bytes, activity <= 64 B, reason <= 1024 B, timeoutMs >= 0, ifAvailable not combined with signal or timeoutMs; refused, never truncated), and name resolution: find-or-claim a name slot by CAS so every thread resolves one name to one slot, with LockCapacityError('names') when full.
acceptanceChecks: createLockBlock stores its capacities in the header and a second installLockManager over the same block reads the same layout
Each invalid argument is refused with LockArgumentError naming the argument and limit, before any shared state changes
Resolving the same name twice returns the same slot; a full name table gives LockCapacityError naming the names table
getLockManager() without an install returns a manager over a private block

tasks.title: request: grant, release on settle, ifAvailable, writer preference, nesting, test hooks
tasks.summary: Implement LockManager.request for grants without waiting: every change to a name's state happens inside its per-name mutex (CAS 0 -> threadId, a few atomic writes, never across an await); exclusive is granted only when the lock word is 0, shared only when it is >= 0 and no exclusive is pending; the holder slot is claimed by CAS 0 -> -1, filled (mode, threadId, acquisition id, since, metadata) and published last as name index + 1 before the callback runs; a full holder table gives back the lock word and throws LockCapacityError('holders'). The callback runs in try/finally and release (lock word, holder slot cleared, version bumped, notify) happens on resolve, reject or synchronous throw. ifAvailable grants now or calls back with (null, blockedBy) listing holders and, for shared, pending exclusive requests, without registering as pending. An AsyncLocalStorage set of held names refuses a same-name re-request and an unbounded nested wait for another name with LockNestedError. A test-only grant hook (set through an exported setter, a no-op by default) is called at three points: inside the critical section, after the lock word changes, and before the holder record is published, so integration tests can pause and terminate a worker mid-grant.
acceptanceChecks: Exclusive excludes exclusive and shared, shared admits shared, and mode defaults to exclusive
ifAvailable returns callback(null, blockedBy) with the holders and their metadata when unavailable and leaves no pending entry
The lock is released and its holder slot cleared after resolve, reject and a synchronous throw, and the error is rethrown unchanged
A same-name nested request and a nested different-name request with neither ifAvailable nor timeoutMs fail with LockNestedError; a nested different name with ifAvailable or timeoutMs is allowed
A full holder table gives LockCapacityError naming holders and leaves the lock word unchanged
The grant hook fires at its three points in order when set and changes nothing when unset

tasks.title: Waiting requests: pending table, waitAsync, timeout, abort, arrival order
tasks.summary: Add the waiting path to request: a pending slot (claim -1, publish name index + 1 last) with mode, threadId and since; an exclusive waiter increments the pending-exclusive count under the name's mutex from the moment it starts waiting until it is granted, times out or aborts (writer preference), and the count and the lock word are read and changed only under that mutex so a shared grant never interleaves with an exclusive waiter registering; waiters wait with Atomics.waitAsync on the version word with a keep-alive timer, never Atomics.wait; timeoutMs rejects with LockTimeoutError carrying name, waitedMs and holders; a signal aborted before queuing rejects with signal.reason before touching shared state, and an abort while waiting cleans up and rejects with signal.reason; clean-up removes the pending slot, decrements the count and bumps the version. Requests for one name from one thread are served in arrival order through a per-thread queue; a full pending table gives LockCapacityError('pending').
acceptanceChecks: A waiting exclusive request is granted when the holder releases, and while it waits a new ifAvailable shared request gets null with it in blockedBy and a waiting shared request runs only after it

tasks.title: query, reclaim and watchWorker
tasks.summary: Implement query() as a synchronous lock-free read of held and pending slots that reads a slot only when its state is published (> 0), so a slot being written is omitted but never torn; reclaim(threadId) on the main thread takes over any name mutex whose value is the dead threadId, removes that thread's holder and pending records, recomputes each affected name's lock word and pending-exclusive count from the remaining published records, releases the mutex, bumps the version and notifies, resets name slots left 'being claimed' by that thread to free, and logs each reclaimed entry as a warning with name, mode and metadata; watchWorker(worker) captures worker.threadId at registration and calls reclaim with it on 'exit'. Unit tests prove mutex takeover and name-claim reset by writing a foreign threadId into the mutex and name state words directly; the real-termination proof is t6's.
acceptanceChecks: query() lists held and pending entries with mode, threadId, since and metadata, and omits metadata when none was given

With a foreign threadId written into a name's mutex word and a name slot's claim state, reclaim(that threadId) takes over the mutex, recounts, and resets the claim to free
watchWorker reclaims using the threadId captured at registration

tasks.title: Cross-thread integration tests with real workers
tasks.summary: Add a helper worker script under src/shared/locks/__tests__/helpers that runs scripted lock operations (request with options, hold until told, release, query, nested requests, and the t2 grant hook set to pause at a chosen point) and reports outcomes, and an integration test file proving the semantics across threads sharing one block: main shared vs worker ifAvailable exclusive, wake within 50 ms of release, writer preference across three workers, reclaim of a terminated holder and waiter, metadata read across threads, startDaemonWorker sharing the lock with the main thread, opposite-order nested bounded waits ending in one LockTimeoutError, watchWorker reclaiming without an explicit call, and termination at each point of a grant leaving nothing held.
